description_full: Progress Software Corporation provides software products that develops, deploys, and manages artificial intelligence (AI) powered applications and digital experiences in the United States and internationally. The company offers Agentic RAG, a next-generation Agentic Rag-as-a-Service platform; Automate MFT, a cloud-native Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform for automated and secure file transfers; Chef, a DevOps/DevSecOps automation software; Corticon, a decision automation platform; DataDirect, a secure data connectivity tools for Relational, NoSQL, Big Data, and SaaS data sources; Developer Tools, such as software development tooling collection, including NET and JavaScript UI components for web, desktop and mobile applications, AI-prompt components, reporting and report management tools, and automated testing and mocking tools; Flowmon, a AI-powered network security and visibility product with automated response across hybrid cloud ecosystems; and Kemp LoadMaster, an application delivery and security product for cloud-native, and virtual and hardware load balancers. It also provides MarkLogic, a data agility platform to connect data and metadata; MOVEit, a managed file transfer software; OpenEdge, an application development platform; Semaphore, a Semantic AI platform; ShareFile, an SaaS-native AI-powered document centric collaboration platform; Sitefinity, a digital experience platform foundation; and WhatsUp Gold, a network infrastructure monitoring software to find and fix network problems. The company offers project management, implementation, custom software development, programming, and other services, as well as web-enable applications, and training services. It sells its products to end users, independent software vendors, original equipment manufacturers, system integrators, value added resellers, and distributors. The company was founded in 1981 and is headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: Progress Software Corporation is a small-cap technology business with a $1.8B market cap on $978M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +18% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 13% against a 8% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $229M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 8.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 6.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.3% of the shares.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 9pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-8.1% a year).

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 11% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 7% over the last three months.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 8% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 54% and a beta of 0.78, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.64 vs 5y 0.69), so read it loosely.
About $18.6M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 39% in the 2020 crash, 20% in the 2022 bear market and 56% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 61% below its DCF fair value of $111, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 22%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $66.46 to $183 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 20.0 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 8.8 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 7.7 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 27% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 12.9% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 5 covering analysts target $56.20 on average, 29% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.58).
It runs a 83% gross margin and converts 23% of revenue into free cash flow, or 17% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 3.22x.
ROE of 15% is amplified by 5.1x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 6.6% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 8.2x net debt to EBITDA ($94.8M of cash against $1.4B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.2x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.02 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.49 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 53% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 17.5% over 3 years, 17.2% over 5 years and 10.0% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 10.7% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.05, a backlog worth 55% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 5%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 0.6% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 34, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.3%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $1.5M sold).
It returns 6.0% a year to shareholders (5.9% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 16.8% of the float, 7.0 days to cover.
people: With about 2,801 employees, each generates about $349K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 4.2% a year.
That works out to $82K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.7M (5x revenue per employee).
